status: Prospective US household-purchase design before any US spending response fit
author: Amanjeet Singh
question: Does forecast-purged monetary tightening leave a cumulative shortfall in real durable purchases over the following three years?
country_selection: Direct household purchase measures, a longer published policy record and observed pre-decision forecasts; selected before US outcome estimation

sample.rule: All original source events with DTARG, all 18 purge inputs and RESID observed. No imputation or undefined-shock substitution.
sample.common_rows: All consumption horizons, categories and policy-lag comparisons use the same 238 complete events from January 1971. This permits 24 genuinely observed prior monthly intentions from January 1969; pre-coverage monthly zeros are not policy observations. Macro-history and 36-month follow-up must be complete

treatment.name: Forecast-controlled innovation in intended funds-rate policy
treatment.units: Annual percentage points; positive is intended tightening
treatment.reconstruction: DTARG minus the complete source 19-column forecast design times its least-squares coefficient. Verify supplied RESID.
treatment.interpretation: A policy-intentions innovation and its ensuing endogenous policy path under maintained source information and response assumptions; not a permanent externally imposed rate path

primary.timing: t is the decision calendar month. Start with the next full calendar month. Denominator uses the last full pre-decision month.
primary.units: Months of the pre-decision real purchase flow, per 25-basis-point intended-policy innovation
primary.null: Cumulative response equals zero; two-sided alpha .05
primary.counterfactual: Subtracting 36 is a units baseline absorbed by the intercept, not an assumption of flat no-shock purchases

conditioning.past_real_transforms: Monthly and trailing twelve-month 100 log growth, both measured at t-1 for each of the four real series
conditioning.other_past_states: Annual 100 log PCE inflation at t-1 and monthly effective funds-rate level at t-1
conditioning.policy_history: Twelve lags of monthly raw DTARG from the original author monthly sheet; use documented raw intentions rather than generated lagged shocks
conditioning.forecast_timing: Each event retains its own genuinely pre-meeting source forecasts. Do not sum later within-month forecasts into controls for an earlier decision.
conditioning.generated_proxy: Since all current source purge columns are included, exact partial-regression invariance removes dependence on estimated current purge coefficients. It does not establish exogeneity or correct source measurement.

inference.method: OLS joint influence scores; sum all same-month event scores before Bartlett calendar-HAC
inference.bandwidth_reason: 35 months of overlap in 36 full monthly purchase flows, plus a fixed six-month dependence buffer
inference.finite_correction: n/(n-k), where n is event observations and k is design rank
inference.critical_values: Asymptotic standard normal, with explicit finite-sample qualification
inference.primary_interval: 95 per cent two-sided pointwise interval for the single declared durable C36 outcome
inference.endpoint_family: Bonferroni .05/9 for the three cumulative windows (first12, later24, full36) in each of three categories
inference.profile_family: A separate Bonferroni .05/36 family for each category, covering its 36 cumulative monthly endpoints on common rows and bandwidth 41; no joint 108-endpoint coverage claim

companions.identity: full36=first12+later24 in coefficients and influence scores; use joint covariance, never combine marginal intervals
companions.flow_profile: Monthly real purchase-level response 100*(Q[t+h]/Q[t-1]-1), h=1..36, expressed as a percentage of the pre-decision flow, not a percentage of a growing future counterfactual; no inference of full recovery from non-rejection
companions.quantity_measure: Official chain quantity indexes. Reference-year nominal anchor and annual-rate factors cancel within each normalised category. Do not add non-additive category chains.

financial_check.window: Mean published daily effective funds rate date+1..+7 less date-7..-1, equal calendar weights, decision day excluded
financial_check.rule: Window fixed before financial relevance or US spending screening; retain all 263 complete source windows, using the declared 238 common analytical rows
financial_check.native_implementation: Estimated overnight-rate response per .25-point intended-policy innovation
financial_check.rate_normalisation: Supplementary ratio of the spending and financial coefficients times .25, with joint HAC Anderson-Rubin inverse 95 per cent set; do not claim intervention on observed DFF
financial_check.measurement: Published historical quotes include repeated non-trading-day observations and documented changes in rate measurement; no interpolation

declared_sensitivities.name: leverage_adjusted_HAC
declared_sensitivities.score_adjustment: Divide each event residual by 1-minus-its-leverage before calendar aggregation

declared_sensitivities.name: event_month_start
declared_sensitivities.purpose: Sensitivity to omitted partial decision month, with pre-month denominator retained

diagnostics.predetermined_outcome: sum(Q[t-j]/Q[t-13] for j=1..12)-12; annual pre-decision durable purchases, same controls and rows
diagnostics.single_event_deletion: All 238 primary durable C36 point estimates; record undefined designs and most influential dates
checks: Common event sample and actual calendar distances
Joint window coefficient and score identities
Financial AR topology and zero-test equivalence

limits: Forecast sufficiency, policy-intentions coding, no omitted policy-correlated news, dynamic sequential restrictions and response stability remain maintained assumptions. A linear signed-shock response imposes symmetric easing and tightening effects. Finite 36-month shortfalls are not lifetime losses or evidence against later purchase reversal. Category contrasts do not isolate a household channel.
